note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: UK: Healey's first Budget DELIVERED Oct 28 — headroom £15B in 2029/30 (vs £23.6B March), OBR 2027 growth cut to 1.0% (from 1.6%), 2026 lifted to 1.2%; gilt 10Y -2bp to 5.323%, sterling $1.3298 — the 'boring budget' bond markets wanted (Reuters/XTB). France: Moody's SPARED France (Aa3 affirmed, neg outlook); OAT-Bund ~167-177bp; revenue-section vote Nov 3; S&P reviews France Nov 27. ECB Oct 29: Lagarde steps down Feb 7, 2027 — succession starts immediately. No US shutdown — CR through Dec 11.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US Q3 GDP advance BEAT: 3.4% SAAR (vs 3.2% consensus, prev 2.2%); claims 194K (vs ~199K) — low-hire, low-fire intact. Overnight: Tokyo CPI in line (core 2.6%), Japan IP BEAT (+2.2% m/m vs +1.3% exp) but retail MISSED (+2.3% y/y vs 3.3% exp), jobs tightened to 2.4%; Australia PPI a touch hot (+1.1% q/q vs 1.0% exp) into the RBA. Fri: EZ/German Q3 GDP + EZ flash CPI, Canada Aug GDP, US ECI (Q3).
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: US Sep PCE in line: headline +0.5% m/m, +3.6% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +3.1% y/y. AU Q3 CPI hotter than the RBA’s path: trimmed +1.0% q/q (Bank forecast 0.8%), Q3 trimmed 3.7% y/y, monthly Sep headline 4.3% y/y (vs 4.2% exp) — Nov hike case firms; Q3 PPI +1.1% q/q adds pipeline heat. Tokyo CPI Oct: core in line at 2.6% y/y (headline 2.8%). EZ flash CPI Fri; German flash CPI Fri. US CPI 3.7%, import prices +8.1% y/y; BoJ trend index 3.2% y/y in Sep (3-yr high, Reuters Oct 27) cements the Dec BoJ case. BoC MPR: Canada inflation 3.5% by end-2026, 3.1% in 2027, back to 2% only by mid-2028.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: FOMC HELD Oct 28 at 3.75-4.00% (10-2; Cook + Hammack for a hike) — December hike ~75-82% into Oct 30 Asia. ECB HELD Oct 29 at 2.50% — Lagarde: direction of travel 'clear', a hike was debated; Reuters sources call a Dec 17 hike 'all but certain'; Lagarde steps down Feb 7, 2027. BoJ HELD Oct 30 at 1.25% (8-1, Takata for 1.50%) — Outlook Report calls the 2% target reached; December hike ~80%; Ueda presser 1:30am CT. BoC HIKED Oct 28 to 2.50% (first since July 2023); December further hike ~45%. RBA Nov 2-3 (hike ~79-85%), BoE Nov 5 (hike ~94%). RBNZ's Oct 28 surprise hold (4-3, 2.75%) delays tightening to Dec 9, not abandons it.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: New CFTC (Oct 20, released Oct 23): euro net short largest since Mar-2020 (contrarian +1 — squeeze side up); hedge funds cut yen shorts, added AUD longs, more bearish CAD (net short largest since early Aug — squeeze fuel into BoC); more bullish GBP. Dollar longs <$40B (down from $44.5B). No crowded-long unwind risk — the pain trade is the euro-short squeeze.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Overnight: AI-led risk-off knocked DXY below 102.00 as the yen held into the BoJ; oil jumped (Brent ~$116) on reports of possible renewed US action on Iran — WSJ: CENTCOM briefed Trump on options Thu; strike-timing claims (Oct 30-31) are single-source and unconfirmed. Houthi claims on Saudi refineries + a Saudi intercept continue; Vance's letter earlier sought to revive Iran talks. Shekel -1% to 3.084 as the Israel count confirmed a deadlock (official results Nov 4). The haven bid is split this time — yen and franc firmer, dollar softer.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent ~$116.14 / WTI ~$103.43 in Asia Fri (price-chart.com Oct 30) — up ~0.6-0.7% on Iran-strike reports; spread ~$12.70. EIA drew -1.9M bbl to 410.6M bbl (week ended Oct 23). Net importers (EUR/JPY) still pay the tax; exporters (AUD/CAD) get the tailwind.
tot.title: Terms of trade
